newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Saadi Cement offers shares.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Saadi Cement offers shares.

text.p: Pakistan's Saadi Cement Ltd on Sunday invited subscription for 10-rupee shares worth a total of 462.5 million rupees ($11.499 million) by March 5.
Analysts said the issue, to raise local funds for a cement plant being built in Haripur, in North West Frontier Province, was likely to prove an attractive long-term investment.
"This is a good time to get in right now as it is one of the best cement plants," said Noman Ali of Taurus Securities Ltd, after a recent visit to the site of the new unit.
Analyst Ali Raza said Pakland Cement Ltd, listed on the Karachi Stock Exchange, has a big stake in Saadi Cement.
"The project's cost will be half that of other plants with the same capacity as it is being set up in a tax-holiday area in northern Pakistan," Raza said.
Saadi Cement has an authorised capital of three billion rupees, of which sponsors have subscribed 1.3875 billion. Total capital after the new issue will be 1.85 billion rupees.
Its stocks will be listed on Pakistan's three bourses soon after successful applicants receive their share certificates.
Brokers have not yet started trading the scrip in the kerb market, Karachi dealer Majid Chapra said.
Saadi Cement Ltd was incorporated in Peshawar on March 19, 1994 to set up a plant in Haripur to manufacture cement based on the dry production process, a company spokesman said.
The plant, with a capacity of 3,600 tonnes a day, is due to start full commercial production in June, he said.
He said per capita cement demand in Pakistan, now estimated at just over 71 kg a year, was expected to surge in future.
Saadi Cement is sponsored by the Pakland Group, which owns Pakland Cement Ltd. Pakland's 10-rupee stock closed 0.25 rupee up at 22.75 at the Karachi Stock Exchange on Thursday.
